labels.OBSERVED: Directly measured or counted from the cited dataset. It is evidence, not automatically a generation quota.
labels.DERIVED RULE: A generation or review constraint logically derived from an OBSERVED fact.
labels.HEURISTIC: A practical safety recommendation or implementation choice not directly measured by the official data.

classification_contract.requirement: Every normative rule in this addendum must carry exactly one of the three labels above. OBSERVED facts must not be silently promoted to hard generation constraints.

source_of_truth.precedence: Structured JSON/CSV artifacts are authoritative over presentation reports if a discrepancy appears.
source_of_truth.tokenization_rule: Unicode-aware lexical tokens: letter/number sequences are words; internal apostrophes and hyphens remain inside one token; punctuation-only tokens are excluded. The same rule is used for sentences, spans, corrections, and gaps.

relationship_to_grammar_spec.we_format_spec_role: how a Written Expression item is physically and linguistically constructed
relationship_to_grammar_spec.integration_mode: additive layer; existing grammar specification is not rewritten

official_counts.basis: Full official 125-item analysis and 500 marked spans.

official_span_position_and_gap.limitation: The official PDF text layer has no reliable exact token offsets; span placement and gap values are ordered token-index approximations.

constraint_policy.statement: Do not convert PDF gap values into over-precise absolute placement constraints.

vocabulary.LONG_PHRASE: 5+ tokens; no official marked span in this sample
vocabulary.CLAUSE_OR_CLAUSE_LIKE: A clause or clause-like unit identified using grammatical role, subtype, or error scope as well as surface length

dimension_separation.rule: Record surface word count and syntactic span type as independent metadata dimensions; do not use one as a substitute for the other.

unmarked_context.format_characteristic: Official items retain natural unmarked linguistic context outside the marked spans.

span_spacing.method: ordered-PDF-geometry approximation using ordered span anchors and token-index approximations
span_spacing.unit: unmarked lexical tokens between successive spans

constraint_note.statement: Use as approximate reference geometry, not an exact absolute placement constraint.

not_single_word_claim.statement: The correct error span is not always one word; multiword and clause-like correct spans are officially observed.

correction_locality.dimension_note: Correction locality records the information required to identify and repair the error; it is not reducible to marked span length.

decision_granularity.dimension_note: A Written Expression-specific design dimension independent of primary_target.

interpretation.rule: A future WE generator and reviewer must evaluate format geometry separately from grammatical validity because grammatical analyzability alone does not ensure an ETS-like Written Expression format.
interpretation.evidence_use: The official-versus-AI mismatch justifies this addendum; it is not itself a grammar taxonomy change.

preferred_range.method: central empirical band derived from the official item-level coverage distribution
preferred_range.note: Quantile choices are a provisional implementation method, not an official threshold.

warning_range.method: values outside preferred range but within observed or plausible tail
warning_range.action: diagnostic warning or reviewer attention; not automatic grammar rejection

extreme_outlier.action: Do not use as the normal generation pattern; flag for format review.

explicit_non_rule.statement: Do not invent a universal hard minimum for unmarked_word_count or a universal hard maximum for span_word_count from this addendum alone.

derived_rules.statement: Model a Written Expression item as one complete sentence with four locally inspectable marked spans and natural unmarked linguistic context.
Do not generate the item as a sentence wholly divided into four answer options; A-D are local marked spans inside the sentence.
Use the sentence-first construction order: natural sentence, syntax/meaning validation, one genuine defect, error location, four spans, three correct-span checks, then geometry diagnostics.
Each marked span must be grammar-relevant, locally identifiable, sentence-distributed, and a plausible candidate for scrutiny.
Record surface word count and syntactic span type independently.
Do not impose an absolute max-2-word or max-3-word marked-span rule; official 4-word spans exist and the correct error span reaches four words.
Treat marked coverage as a distribution-aware property with preferred, warning, and extreme-outlier concepts rather than one arbitrary hard threshold.
Do not use 100% marked coverage as the normal generation pattern.
Retain enough unmarked context to support syntactic dependency, lexical context, sentence naturalness, and meaningful difficulty.
Do not convert approximate PDF gap values into exact absolute placement constraints.
Keep format validity diagnostics separate from grammatical validity and report them in separate result dimensions.
basis: correction locality and decision granularity evidence

derived_rules.statement: Keep correction locality and decision granularity as explicit WE metadata independent of primary_target.

heuristics.statement: Avoid designs in which marked spans cover almost the entire sentence.
heuristics.basis: Official coverage center and unmarked-context profile.

heuristics.statement: Choose exact preferred and warning coverage boundaries using a documented empirical-quantile or equivalent reference-distribution method in Generator v1.2.
heuristics.basis: Coverage policy requires machine-readable derivation but the implementation thresholds are intentionally deferred.

heuristics.statement: Use dependency distance, clause structure, verb frame, subtle morphology, function-word choice, agreement relationships, and plausible-but-incorrect forms as primary difficulty levers.
heuristics.basis: Official correction locality and decision granularity observations plus existing grammar analysis.

heuristics.statement: Use approximate gap medians as diagnostic reference values and batch-shape guidance, not exact token-placement quotas.
Allow occasional tail-format items when the grammatical design is strong, but route extreme geometry outliers to format review.
heuristics.basis: Observed distributions have non-zero tails and small samples cannot be reproduced exactly in every batch.

heuristics.statement: Future reviewer statuses may use independent PASS, WARN, FAIL, and NOT_EVALUATED values for grammar_validity and format_validity; exact status vocabulary is deferred.
heuristics.basis: Need to separate grammatical invalidity from format/style failure.

steps: Create a natural complete academic-style sentence.
Design or inject one genuine grammatical defect.
Select four local spans A-D from the existing sentence.
Verify the other three spans are grammatically acceptable and the corrected sentence has no secondary error.
Run span geometry and distribution diagnostics.
construction_sequence.avoid: Create four marked parts first and join them into a sentence.

sentence_word_count.definition: Lexical word count of the complete sentence using the source tokenization rule.

span_word_counts.definition: Lexical word count of each marked span using the source tokenization rule.

mean_span_length.definition: Arithmetic mean of the four marked span word counts for one item.

max_span_length.definition: Maximum of the four marked span word counts for one item.

marked_coverage_ratio.definition: unique_marked_token_count / sentence_word_count; use unique marked tokens if spans overlap.

gap_A_B.definition: Number of unmarked lexical tokens between the end of A and the start of B. Exact for generated token offsets; approximate for the official PDF reference.

gap_B_C.definition: Number of unmarked lexical tokens between the end of B and the start of C.

gap_C_D.definition: Number of unmarked lexical tokens between the end of C and the start of D.

correct_span_word_count.definition: Lexical word count of the one marked span identified as containing the intended error.

correct_span_type.definition: Syntactic type of the correct/error span, independent of word count.

correction_locality.definition: Information scope required to identify and repair the error.

decision_granularity.definition: Primary level at which the Written Expression decision is made; independent of primary_target.

format_distribution_distance.definition: Distance between an item or batch's format metrics and the official reference profile.

requirements: Construct the complete sentence before selecting A-D.
Maintain exactly four marked spans and one intended erroneous span.
Retain natural unmarked context around and between spans.
Select grammar-relevant, locally inspectable, plausible spans.
Use distribution-aware span lengths without an absolute 2-word or 3-word maximum.
Treat marked coverage as preferred/warning/extreme-outlier diagnostics.
Do not normalize all items to 100% marked coverage.
Record correction_locality and decision_granularity independently of primary_target.
Verify three non-error spans and absence of secondary grammatical errors.
Run geometry diagnostics after grammatical and whole-sentence validation.
heuristic_choices_deferred: Use of gap medians as soft reference values
Routing policy for extreme format outliers

separation_rule.rule: Report format violation separately from grammatical invalidity.

examples.grammatically_valid_but_format_outlier: format/style warning or failure; not automatically a grammar rejection

non_changes_in_this_addendum: No rewrite of existing grammar specification
